A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeXL and contain 30 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and finance regression results, including Tables 1–2 and 8–10.

after.justification: v4 retains the original classification, regression, ablation, and sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 moves validation and checkpoint selection before reflection generation and text refinement, changing which reflection is saved with the encoder. This revises the stated optimization procedure; the architecture, losses, prediction fusion, and Appendix G regression adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Weather, Finance, Healthcare Test-Positive, and Healthcare Mortality classification tasks, plus finance regression in Appendix G.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 8 retain the same 18 baselines, including TimeCAP, MM-PatchTST, and MM-iTransformer. The ablation comparators and alternative LLM backbones also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the encoder-training dataset designation from D_train,i to D_train,val, revising the stated use of validation data. The 6:2:2 split, metrics, and other experimental settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component and objective ablations, regularization and prototype-length sensitivity analyses, explanation-count experiments, iterative studies, backbone comparisons, and classification/regression case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five experimental runs and retain identical uncertainty entries in Tables 4–6. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing changes appear.

E6.justification: All table entries and graphical results match. For example, Weather F1/AUC remain 0.696/0.808, and Table 8 regression RMSE/MAE/MAPE remain 4.161/2.844/2.035. Appendix C retains the same numerical cost estimates; their wording changes without new measurements.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, similarity measures, projection rule, and regression construction are unchanged. Correcting p to p' in the text-prototype retrieval expression and identifying its raw-text counterpart clarify existing notation and prompting, rather than introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about prototype-based explanations, three collaborating LLM agents, four benchmarks, and up to 8.9% AUC improvement.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.2 drops contribution weights from its description of explanation artifacts. Appendix C also qualifies inference latencies as achievable low times ('can take down to') instead of approximate per-sample times, narrowing their deployment interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix C revises the runtime characterization of the unchanged 3.46 seconds/sample for GPT-4o and 2.29 seconds/sample for Gemini-2.0-Flash to attainable low timings. Hyperparameters, model identifiers, hardware, prompt templates, and data-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix H, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to multi-modal prediction, explainability, and LLM-based time-series research.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify prototype terminology, revise reflection-selection and runtime wording, correct 'relf' to 'Refl', and update the arXiv stamp. Section ordering and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 26 figures and 10 tables remain, with unchanged graphical content. Limited spacing and text reflow alter nearby layout, including moving Figure 5 upward on page 9; no figures or tables are redesigned.

improvement.justification: v4 usefully clarifies raw-text prototype inputs, but the reordered Algorithm 1 now checks Refl before its first assignment, and D_train,val leaves the training/validation boundary unclear. All empirical evidence remains unchanged. These clarification benefits and unresolved procedural ambiguities prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
